hook.convey: closed shape → walk its edge from one corner, along every side, back to that same corner → the distance walked = perimeter; a rectangular cricket pitch, the border of a drawing sheet, a fence along a garden bed

use.hi: Cricket pitch ek lamba rectangle hoti hai, lagbhag 20 m lambi aur 3 m chaudi. Pitch ke ek kone se chalna shuru karo, kinaare-kinaare chalo aur wapas usi kone par pahuncho, toh jitni doori tay hui, wahi pitch ka parimap hai.
use.en: A cricket pitch is a long rectangle, about 20 m long and 3 m wide. Start at one corner of the pitch, walk along its edge and come back to the same corner: the distance walked is the pitch's perimeter.

use.hi: Drawing sheet ke chaaron kinaaron par colour ki border banao, toh us border ki poori lambai sheet ka parimap hoti hai.
use.en: If you draw a coloured border along all four edges of a drawing sheet, the full length of that border is the sheet's perimeter.

use.hi: Garden mein phoolon ki kyari ke kinaare par baad lagti hai. Baad kyari ki har bhuja ke saath chalti hai, ek bhi bhuja nahi chhootti.
use.en: In a garden, a fence goes along the edge of a flower bed. The fence runs along every side of the bed; not one side is left out.

explain.convey: perimeter (parimap) = total length of the boundary of a closed shape → start at a corner, go along every side, end back at that corner; triangle 4 cm, 5 cm, 6 cm → all three sides go into the sum

point.hi: Is triangle ki teen bhujayein hain: 4 cm, 5 cm aur 6 cm. Ek kone se chalo, teeno bhujaon se hote hue wapas usi kone par aao. Yeh poora raasta hi triangle ka parimap hai.
point.en: This triangle has three sides: 4 cm, 5 cm and 6 cm. Start at one corner, go along all three sides and come back to the same corner. That whole path is the triangle's perimeter.

prompt.hi: Toh is triangle ka parimap kitna hai?
prompt.en: So what is the perimeter of this triangle?

why.hi: teeno bhujayein judti hain, 4 + 5 + 6 = 15 cm
why.en: all three sides are added, 4 + 5 + 6 = 15 cm

explain.convey: any polygon (bahubhuj) → same rule: add every side, however many; hexagon = 6 sides → 6 lengths in the sum; regular hexagon with only one side labelled 5 cm → the unlabelled sides still belong to the boundary → still added

point.hi: Yeh hexagon hai. Iski chhah bhujayein hain aur sab barabar lambi hain. Label sirf ek bhuja par hai, 5 cm. Baaki bhujaon par kuch likha nahi hai, phir bhi woh kinaare ka hissa hain. Parimap mein har bhuja ki lambai judti hai.
point.en: This is a hexagon. It has six sides and all of them are equally long. Only one side has a label, 5 cm. Nothing is written on the other sides, but they are still part of the edge. In the perimeter every side's length is added.

prompt.hi: Toh is hexagon ka parimap kitna hai?

why.en: the hexagon's six equal sides are 5 cm each, 6 × 5 = 30 cm

explain.convey: perimeter = AROUND the shape (a thread along the edge) → a length → cm, m, km; area (kshetrafal) = INSIDE (tiles covering the surface) → a different quantity; 6 cm by 4 cm rectangle → the edge goes 6, 4, 6, 4 → add them, never 6 × 4

point.hi: Yeh rectangle 6 cm lamba aur 4 cm chauda hai. Parimap ek dhaage jaisa hai jo kinaare par chalta hai: upar 6 cm, phir 4 cm, neeche 6 cm, phir 4 cm. Andar ki jagah area hai, woh bilkul alag cheez hai.
point.en: This rectangle is 6 cm long and 4 cm wide. The perimeter is like a thread running along the edge: 6 cm on top, then 4 cm, 6 cm at the bottom, then 4 cm. The space inside is the area, which is a completely different thing.

prompt.hi: Is rectangle ke kinaare par ek baar dhaaga lagana hai. Kitna dhaaga lagega?

why.en: the thread runs along the edge, 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 cm

Board par 10 m aur 6 m ek-ek baar likha hai, par kinaare par chalte hue lambai do baar aati hai aur chaudai bhi do baar.
point.en: In this rectangle the top and bottom sides are 10 m; that is the length. The right and left sides are 6 m; that is the breadth. Opposite sides are equal. The board writes 10 m and 6 m once each, but walking the edge you pass the length twice and the breadth twice.

prompt.hi: Toh is rectangle ka parimap kitna hai?

why.en: along the edge the length comes twice and the breadth twice, 10 + 6 + 10 + 6 = 32 m

explain.convey: one length + one breadth = corner to the opposite corner = HALF the way round; the full round = that half twice → P = 2 × (l + b); on a new 12 m by 5 m rectangle the child does 2 × (12 + 5) = 34 m; l + b alone = 17 m = only half the boundary

point.hi: Yeh rectangle 12 m lamba aur 5 m chauda hai. Neeche baayein kone se chalo: 12 m lambai, phir 5 m chaudai, aur tum saamne wale kone par ho. Yeh sirf aadha raasta hai. Baaki aadha raasta bhi utna hi hai. Isliye rectangle ka parimap = 2 × (lambai + chaudai).
point.en: This rectangle is 12 m long and 5 m wide. Start at the bottom-left corner: 12 m of length, then 5 m of breadth, and you are at the opposite corner. That is only half the way. The other half is just as long. So a rectangle's perimeter = 2 × (length + breadth).

prompt.hi: Is rectangle ki lambai 12 m aur chaudai 5 m hai. 2 × (lambai + chaudai) se iska parimap kitna hai?

point.hi: Yeh square hai. Iski chaaron bhujayein 6 cm ki hain, sab barabar. Chaar baar 6 cm jodne ki jagah seedha 4 × bhuja kar sakte ho. Jawab ek lambai hai, isliye cm mein aayega, square cm mein nahi.
point.en: This is a square. All four of its sides are 6 cm, all equal. Instead of adding 6 cm four times, you can just do 4 × side. The answer is a length, so it comes in cm, not square cm.

point.en: This square's perimeter is 60 m, and that 60 m is shared by four equal sides. So to find one side we divide the perimeter by 4, not by 2.

point.en: This rectangular plot is 12 m long and 8 m wide. The wire goes along the whole edge, so the perimeter is 2 × (12 + 8) = 40 m. Wire is ₹10 per metre, so the cost is 40 × 10 = ₹400. On the board, one side of the plot has a 2 m gate. No wire goes on a gate, so we first subtract its length from the perimeter, then multiply.

backward for a rectangle: perimeter and length known → halve, then subtract the length

remediation.move: ant walk run backward: full boundary = 2 lengths + 2 breadths; the ant at the opposite corner = half the perimeter = 1 length + 1 breadth; 18 m by 12 m → 60 m round, half = 30 m = 18 + 12 → so halve the perimeter first, then take away the length

say.hi: Is rectangle ki lambai 18 m aur chaudai 12 m hai. Poora chakkar do lambai aur do chaudai, 60 m. Saamne wale kone tak aadha raasta hai, 30 m, yaani 18 + 12. Isliye ulta chalte waqt pehle parimap ka aadha karo, phir lambai ghatao.
say.en: This rectangle is 18 m long and 12 m wide. A full round is two lengths and two breadths, 60 m. The opposite corner is halfway, 30 m, that is 18 + 12. So going backwards, first halve the perimeter, then take away the length.

remediation.move: wire is bought by the metre of edge, not by the ground inside: thread around the plot vs tiles inside it; cost = edge length (m) × ₹ per m; l × b = ground covered, not wire

say.hi: Is rectangle plot ki lambai 10 m aur chaudai 6 m hai. Taar kinaare par lagti hai, toh pehle kinaare ki poori lambai metre mein nikalo, phir har metre ke daam se guna karo. 10 × 6 = 60 andar ki zameen hai, taar nahi.
say.en: This rectangular plot is 10 m long and 6 m wide. Wire goes along the edge, so first find the edge's full length in metres, then multiply by the price per metre. 10 × 6 = 60 is the ground inside, not the wire.

prompt.hi: ₹20 per metre wali taar 9 m lambe aur 6 m chaude plot ke kinaare par ek baar lagti hai. Taar ka kharcha kitna hai?
prompt.en: Wire costing ₹20 per metre goes once around a plot 9 m long and 6 m wide. What does the wire cost?

why.hi: taar kinaare par lagti hai, 2 × (9 + 6) = 30 m, aur 30 × 20 = ₹600
why.en: the wire goes along the edge, 2 × (9 + 6) = 30 m, and 30 × 20 = ₹600
